title: Induction, restriction, and Mackey theory for finite groups, Part II: reduced Schur covers and marked extensions
summary: Starting after the ordinary Schur covers of the induction and restriction roadmap, construct the reduced integral multiplier and its cover-dependent extension. Identify the universal marked extension by its presentation and chosen fiber-product model. Build the discrete power action, exact fixed-fiber obstruction and finite parity algorithms, and compatible reduced covers for coprime semidirect products. These algebraic interfaces supply arithmetic statistics and Hurwitz-space consumers without rebuilding their geometric or counting theories.
readme: This continuation starts at parent Layer 7, not at induction or Mackey decomposition. All 75 incoming paper items are inventoried under one canonical ID. Integral H₂ and cohomological factor-set H² remain distinct. The reader document pins all choices, hypotheses, APIs and acceptance tests; source-reported finite tables require certificates. Ordinary covers come from the parent and generic homological machinery from the precisely recorded missing-supplier request. The discrete action is a set action on U and restricts to automorphisms on its central kernel. Degree lattices have integer coordinates; nonnegative bounds belong to explicit slices. See research/blueprint/readmes/InductionRestrictionPartII.md.

stages.title: Commuting-pair classes and reduced Schur covers
stages.description:
**Commutator of lifts.** For a central GroupExtension A E G, commuting x,y∈G, and arbitrary lifts X,Y∈E, define κ_E(x,y)∈A by inl(κ_E(x,y))=XYX⁻¹Y⁻¹. Surjectivity supplies lifts, exactness gives kernel membership, and injectivity supplies a unique preimage. Centrality means inl(A)⊆Z(E).

**The oriented commuting-pair cycle.** For xy=yx, [x|y]−[y|x] with integral coefficient 1 belongs to groupHomology.cycles₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ). The orientation is x followed by y.

**Universal homological commutator.** For commuting x,y∈G define ⟨x,y⟩ as H2π applied to the oriented cycle [x|y]−[y|x], in M(G)=H₂(G,ℤ). Equivalently it is the image of the oriented generator of H₂(ℤ²,ℤ) under (a,b)↦xᵃyᵇ.

**Schur commutator relations.** For conjugacy-invariant c⊆G set Q_c to the additive subgroup of M(G) generated by ⟨x,y⟩ with x∈c and y∈C_G(x). No generation or rationality hypothesis on c is needed for this quotient.

**Reduced Schur multiplier.** Define M(G,c)=H₂(G,c)=M(G)/Q_c as the additive group quotient of the existing integral H₂ carrier. It depends functorially on (G,c) under f(c)⊆d and is independent of a Schur-cover choice.

**Reduced Schur cover.** Given a chosen ordinary Schur cover π:S→G and its oriented class isomorphism τ_S:M(G)≅kerπ, define S_c=S/τ_S(Q_c). Retain π, τ_S and the cover choice as parameters. The descended π_c:S_c→G is a central surjection with kernel canonically identified with M(G,c) for these data.

**Centralizers lift commutatively.** In a reduced cover S_c→G, if x∈c and y∈C_G(x), any lifts X,Y commute. Consequently C_{S_c}(X)→C_G(x) is surjective.

**Conjugacy classes lift bijectively.** Every conjugacy class in S_c with image contained in c∪{1} maps bijectively to its image conjugacy class in G. No uniqueness is asserted for which class above a class of c is chosen.

**Conjugacy-equivariant lifted marking.** For one representative x_d in each d∈D=c/G, choose a lift X_d∈S_c. Define x̂ for x=gx_dg⁻¹ by a lifted conjugator g̃X_dg̃⁻¹. This is independent of g and g̃ but retains the initial representative-lift choices.

**Local class normalization.** Assume c is one conjugacy class, choose c₀∈c, and let E=S_c. For e with π_c(e)∈c∪{1}, define z(e) to be the unique element in its conjugacy class mapping to c₀ if π_c(e)∈c, and e itself if π_c(e)=1.

**Local normalized factors commute.** Any two elements of a central extension mapping to {1,c₀} commute. In particular all z(e) in the preceding single-class construction commute.

**Reduced-cover homology image.** For π_c:S_c→G, im(H₂(S_c,ℤ)→M(G))=Q_c. Thus the composite H₂(S_c,ℤ)→M(G)→M(G,c) is zero. The equality uses the central-extension homological five-term exact sequence; the zero composite alone also follows by UCT naturality and the diagonal splitting.

**Reduced-cover homology composite vanishes.** The composite H₂(S_c,ℤ)→M(G)→M(G,c) is zero.

**Commuting-pair classes respect orders.** For commuting x,y, the homological commutator is additive in each commuting cyclic variable: ⟨x^n,y⟩=n⟨x,y⟩. In particular if x is an involution then 2⟨x,y⟩=0.

stages.title: Universal marked central extensions
stages.description:
**Marked central extension.** For conjugacy-invariant generating c⊆G, a c-marked central extension is a GroupExtension A E G with central kernel and a section s:c→E such that s(gxg⁻¹)=e s(x)e⁻¹ whenever π(e)=g. Its marked subset s(c) maps bijectively to c. A morphism is a group homomorphism over G preserving s; a kernel identification need not be fixed.

**Universal marked presentation.** For conjugacy-invariant generating c⊆G, U(G,c) is PresentedGroup on the subtype c, with relation words [x][y][x]⁻¹[xyx⁻¹]⁻¹ for x,y∈c. Write [x] for the canonical generator. The map π_U:U→G sends [x] to x.

**Conjugation by a marked word.** For w=[g₁]^a₁⋯[g_k]^a_k and x∈c, w[x]w⁻¹=[π_U(w)xπ_U(w)⁻¹]. The inverse word is [g_k]^−a_k⋯[g₁]^−a₁.

**The presentation is a central extension.** If c generates G, π_U is onto and kerπ_U⊆Z(U); x↦[x] is a conjugacy-equivariant section on c.

**Universal marked central extension.** For every c-marked central extension E→G there is exactly one marked morphism U(G,c)→E. Therefore any two universal marked extensions are uniquely isomorphic through their markings.

**The class degree homomorphism.** Let D=c/G and L=D→₀ℤ. Define δ:L→Additive(G^ab) by δ(e_d)=Additive.ofMul(Abelianization.of(x_d)); conjugate representatives give the same value. It is onto when c generates G.

**The marked fiber product.** For a chosen reduced cover S_c→G, define P=S_c×_{G^ab}Multiplicative(ℤ^D), the subgroup of S_c×Multiplicative L of pairs (h,m) with [π_c(h)]=δ(m). Give it the marking x↦(x̂,e_[x]) from the class-compatible lifts.

**Commutators of the marked fiber product.** [P,P]=[S_c,S_c]×{0}, as a subgroup of S_c×Multiplicative L.

**Abelianization of the marked fiber product.** The degree projection induces P^ab≅Multiplicative(ℤ^D), taking the class of (x̂,e_[x]) to e_[x].

**Abelianization of the presentation.** The degree map identifies U(G,c)^ab with Multiplicative(ℤ^D).

**Split the marked pullback extension.** For a marked central extension E→G, its pullback along P→G has a group-homomorphic splitting. This statement allows arbitrary abelian kernel A, including the infinite kernel of U→G.

**Marking-preserving splitting correction.** Suppose φ:P→E is a homomorphism over G and φ(x̂,e_[x])=s(x)k_x with k_x∈A. The discrepancy depends only on [x]. Let ψ:P→A be the homomorphism factoring through deg:P→ℤ^D with ψ(e_[x])=k_x. Define φ_corr(p)=φ(p) inl(ψ(p))⁻¹.

**The fiber product is universal marked.** For every marked E→G there is a unique marked morphism P→E.

**Presentation and fiber-product comparison.** There is a unique marked isomorphism U(G,c)≅P sending [x] to (x̂,e_[x]), compatible with projections and degree. It transports changes of cover and marking choice through the presentation; no canonical isomorphism S_c≅S′_c is asserted.

**Kernel of the universal marked extension.** Define K(G,c)=ker(π_U:U→G), using the existing kernel subgroup. Under U≅P it is M(G,c)×ker(δ:L→G^ab). It is central and commutative, even though U generally is not. There is an exact sequence 0→M(G,c)→K→kerδ→0.

**Degree of a marked word.** Define deg:U(G,c)→Multiplicative(ℤ^D) by deg([x])=e_[x]. It is a group homomorphism with δ(deg(u)) the abelianized image of π_U(u).

stages.title: Discrete power actions and twisted degree sets
stages.description:
**Finite power action.** Let G be finite, p prime with p∤|G| (or characteristic zero). A unit α of the prime-to-p profinite integers acts on the underlying set of G by g↦g^a, where a is its coordinate modulo ord(g). This is independent of the integer representative and factors through units modulo any positive common exponent of G.

**Power permutation of class degrees.** Assume c is also closed under invertible powers. Powering induces a permutation d↦d^α of D=c/G. Define m^α on L=ℤ^D by m^α(d^α)=m(d); it is a coordinate permutation, not multiplication of each integer coordinate by α.

**Central power correction.** Fix class-compatible marked lifts x̂ in S_c. For a class d with representative x_d define z_d(α)=x̂_d^−α · widehat(x_d^α)∈A=M(G,c). Extend to W_α:L→A by W_α(m)=∏_d z_d(α)^m(d). Powers of finite-cover elements are read at a finite residue level, whereas m(d) remains an integer.

**Composition law for central corrections.** W_{αβ}(m)=W_β(m)^α W_α(m^β) for all m∈L.

**Discrete cyclotomic action.** For P=S_c×_{G^ab}L define α*(h,m)=(h^α W_α(m),m^α). This defines a group action on the underlying set P, and hence on U through the marked comparison. Its projection to G is the ordinary power permutation and its degree projection is the class-degree permutation.

**The restricted kernel action is multiplicative.** Each unit acts by a group automorphism on K(G,c). In cover coordinates h lies in the commutative central A, so α*(hh′,m+m′)=α*(h,m)α*(h′,m′). This statement does not extend to all U.

**A finite level determines the discrete action.** For a finite G, α≡β modulo |G|² implies α* and β* agree on every element of U(G,c). The same holds for K and its degree lattice.

**Cyclotomic twist of a set.** For a unit group B, a nonempty simply transitive B-set T and a B-set X, define X⟨−1⟩=Map_B(T,X), the set of equivariant functions. Evaluation at a chosen t₀∈T is a bijection to X; this bijection depends on t₀. For the papers T is the torsor of topological generators of prime-to-characteristic roots of unity.

**Bounded total-degree slice.** For finite D, n∈ℕ and M∈ℕ define L_{n,≥M}={m∈ℤ^D: every m(d)≥M and Σ m(d)=n}. Define K_{n,≥M} as its degree preimage and the twisted slice as equivariant functions valued in this invariant subset. For the notation of LWZB M is positive; M=0 is also allowed for component tuples.

**Power-fixed degree lattice.** For q prime to |G| define L_{≡q}={m∈ℤ^D:m(d^q)=m(d) for all d}. Its n,≥M slice adds the lower-bound and exact total-degree conditions.

**Orbit set of class degrees.** Define 𝔖^{c,G} as the orbit quotient of the integer lattice L under the unit-power coordinate permutation. Its n,≥M subset is the image of L_{n,≥M}. Choice of a roots-of-unity generator changes a degree vector within this orbit.

stages.title: Fixed fibers and the parity obstruction
stages.description:
**Lift squares are central.** Assume c consists of involutions. For x∈c every lift X∈S_c has X²∈A=M(G,c), hence X² commutes with S_c.

**Square-class obstruction of a fiber.** Assume finite G is generated by involution classes c_i, A=M(G,c), chosen class lifts X_i, and g∈c∪{1} with lift Y (Y=1 for g=1). For an integer degree m with Σ_i m_i[c_i]=[g] in G^ab, define b(g,m)=Y²∏_i(X_i²)^−m_i∈A and β(g,m) as its class in TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient A. Lift changes multiply b by a square; β depends only on the parity of m.

**The fixed-fiber power equation.** For the hypotheses of square-obstruction and odd q coprime to |G|, let r=(q−1)/2. Writing a fiber point as (Yh,m), the q-fixed equation is h^{q−1}=b(g,m)^{−r}. Since the power subgroup is closed under inversion, solvability is equivalent to b(g,m)^r∈A^{2r}.

**All fixed fibers and their torsion count.** For odd q>1 prime to |G|, the fiber over (g,m) has |A[q−1]| fixed points if δ(m)=[g] and b(g,m)^r∈A^{2r}, and zero otherwise. The q and q⁻¹ actions have the same fixed points. No nonnegativity of m is needed for this group-theoretic statement.

**Odd-parity fixed-point fiber.** If g∈c_k, m_k is odd and all other m_i are even, then the fiber is compatible and its fixed count is |A[q−1]|.

**Even-parity fixed-point fiber.** If g=1 and every m_i is even, then the compatible fiber has exactly |A[q−1]| fixed points.

**Square-times-torsion solvability.** For a commutative group A, b∈A and r≥1, b^r∈A^{2r} iff b∈A²·A[r].

**Torsion-image filtration.** For a finite abelian A let B=TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient A. Define B_t to be the image in B of A[2^t]=ker(powMonoidHom(2^t)), regarded as a ZMod 2 subspace. B_0=0; the filtration is increasing and B_e=B when the 2-primary exponent is 2^e.

**Two-primary obstruction threshold.** For b∈finite abelian A with 2-primary exponent 2^e define t_A(b)=min{t≥0: the class of b belongs to B_t}. It lies between 0 and e. It depends only on the square class, and equals the largest cyclic 2-primary exponent among factors where b has odd coordinate (empty maximum 0).

**Two-adic criterion for fiber survival.** For odd q>1 prime to |G| and compatible degree m, the fixed fiber is nonempty iff v₂(q−1)≥t_A(b(g,m))+1.

**Involution classes span the abelianization.** If c consists of N generating involution classes, G^ab is an elementary abelian 2-group. There is a surjective F₂-linear map a:F₂^N→Additive(G^ab), a(e_i)=[c_i].

**Lift-square class columns.** For each involution class c_i, the class s_i of X_i² in B=A/A² is independent of both the lift and the representative in c_i.

**The parity and lift-square maps.** With V=F₂^N, the already constructed a:V→Additive(G^ab), and B=TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient A, define s:V→B by the lift-square columns s(e_i)=s_i. Extend only on the free vector space, not on G or S_c.

**Compatible parities and their obstruction.** For g=1 set v_g=0; for g∈c_k set v_g=e_k. Compatible ε are exactly v_g+ker a, and β(g,ε)=s(v_g+ε).

**Joint parity constraint map.** For t≥0 define the linear map L_t:V→U⊕(B/B_t), v↦(a(v),s(v) mod B_t). Its kernel consists of degree parities compatible with the identity and with square obstruction in B_t.

**Surviving parities form an affine kernel coset.** If v₂(q−1)=t+1, the parities giving nonempty fixed fibers are C_t^g=v_g+kerL_t. Each corresponding compatible integer-degree fiber has |A[q−1]| fixed points.

**Ranks count surviving parities.** |C_t^g|=2^{N−rankL_t}. For K_t=2^{N−rankL_t} and K_{−1}=0, the number of compatible parities with exact threshold t is K_t−K_{t−1}. Real and imaginary signatures have equal parity cardinalities, without an asserted equality of weights.

**Weight enumerator of a surviving parity coset.** For C_t^g⊆F₂^N and lower bound N₀≥0, set δ=N₀ mod 2 and W_t^g(X)=Σ_{ε∈C_t^g} X^{wt(ε+δ·1)}∈ℕ[X]. The exponent is the excess above the coordinate lower bound of the least nonnegative degree of parity ε.

**Independent class images eliminate the obstruction.** If the N class images in G^ab are linearly independent, then a is an isomorphism. Each g-signature has the sole compatible parity v_g, β=0, and a nonempty fixed fiber for every allowed q.

stages.title: Compatible covers of coprime semidirect products
stages.description:
**Split projections induce homology surjections.** For finite G=H⋊Γ, the projection ρ:G→Γ has a section, hence ρ_*:M(G)→M(Γ) is onto.

**Primary parts of a coprime semidirect multiplier.** For finite H,Γ with coprime orders and G=H⋊Γ, M(G) is finite of exponent dividing |G|. Its canonical primary decomposition M_H×M_Γ uses primes dividing |H| and primes dividing |Γ|.

**The coprime central splitting is unique.** For the chosen Schur cover S→H⋊Γ, write S′ as the preimage of H. The central extension 1→M_Γ→S′/M_H→H→1 has a unique splitting and is isomorphic to M_Γ×H.

**The Hall preimage is normal in the cover.** Let φ:S′/M_H→M_Γ be the projection obtained from the unique splitting, and D its kernel preimage in S′. Then D is characteristic in S′, normal in S, and |D|=|H||M_H|.

**Compatible Schur covers.** For finite H,Γ of coprime orders and G=H⋊Γ, choose a Schur cover S→G and let S_Γ=S/D with D from the preceding construction. The quotient S→S_Γ covers G→Γ. The lower central extension has kernel M_Γ and is an ordinary Schur cover of Γ.

**The multiplier-map kernel is H-primary.** For these finite coprime semidirect products, ker(M(G)→M(Γ))≅M_H and its order is prime to |Γ|. The paper states admissibility too; the inspected cover proof uses only finiteness and coprime orders.

**Admissible equal-order inertia classes.** Assume H is generated by h⁻¹γ(h) for h∈H,γ∈Γ (finite admissibility). In G=H⋊Γ let c consist of nonidentity elements having the same order as their image in Γ. Then c generates G, is conjugacy- and invertible-power-stable, and c/G→(Γ∖{1})/Γ is a bijection.

**Admissible semidirect abelianization.** For such admissible H, projection G^ab→Γ^ab is an isomorphism, and the class-lattice maps δ correspond under the bijection c/G≅(Γ∖{1})/Γ.

**The Schur relation map is surjective.** For the c above and d=Γ∖{1}, the split projection sends Q_c onto Q_d.

**Compatible reduced multipliers.** The induced M(G,c)→M(Γ,d) is surjective with H-primary kernel, so its kernel order is prime to |Γ|. The compatible cover map descends to S_c→(S_Γ)_d and commutes with the reduced-kernel isomorphisms.

**Compatibility of power corrections.** Choose class representatives and marked lifts compatible with S_c→(S_Γ)_d. For every unit α, its reduced-kernel map f satisfies f(W^G_α(m))=W^Γ_α(classMap(m)). The marked U and K maps intertwine the discrete actions.

stages.title: Certified reduced multipliers and finite parity algorithms
stages.description:
**Centralizer generators suffice for reduction.** For a central extension E→G, the subgroup generated by all κ_E(x,y) with x∈c,y∈C_G(x) equals that generated using one representative per class in c and any group-generating set of its centralizer.

**Finite reduced-cover certificate.** A certificate for explicit finite groups E,G and π:E→G contains executable multiplication/inverse tables, a surjective homomorphism π, centrality of its kernel, an independently checked ordinary Schur-cover certificate (stem plus maximal kernel/class-map isomorphism), class representatives for c, generating sets for their centralizers, and the subgroup R generated by their lift commutators. Its conclusion identifies A=kerπ/R with M(G,c). Raw GAP output does not supply the cover certificate.

**Finite reduced-cover parity algorithm.** Given a checked reduction certificate, a generating involution c, π₀:G→C₂ and an outside involution τ, compute the class columns a,s, the torsion-image spaces B_t, both cosets C_t^1 and C_t^τ, their ranks, exact-threshold histograms and lower-bound weight enumerators. The algorithm is finite and exact conditional on the certified ordinary cover and explicit marked embedding.

**Odd-index-two homology reduction.** For finite H normal in G with |H| odd and G/H=C₂, M(G)≅M(H)_{C₂} and M(G) has odd order. For any union c of involution classes, Q_c=0 and M(G,c)=M(G).

**The order-96 A₄ arithmetic type.** Let ab:A₄→C₃ be its abelianization map. Put K=ker((a,b)↦ab(a)+ab(b)) inside A₄², and F=K⋊C₂ with the involution swapping the two A₄ factors. Then |K|=48 and |F|=96. Use the explicit embedding F⊆A₄≀C₂ and c its outside order-2 elements for the reduced multiplier, rather than an unmarked abstract SmallGroups label.

**Reduced multiplier of the order-96 type.** For the explicitly embedded order-96 type above with outside-involution c, M(F,c)≅C₂, as reported in Wood Table 2 and Appendix A.1. The formal identification requires an explicit certified cover and relation subgroup; the reported GAP kernel C₂³ and relation subgroup of order 4 remain evidence until certified.
